clue.text: LA Times first with leader on silly municipal regulations

indicators.note: tells you the LA follows the word for 'times', which goes first

parts.note: 'times' as in multiplication: three by four
taken as printed

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
its leader, the first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper's front page leads on some foolish new city rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics dress the first two words as the Los Angeles newspaper; ignore them, because 'times' works as the multiplication word, as in three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: Bylaws are the regulations a local council makes for its own area.

clue.text: Most of rear end and pecs area is maximally macho

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter is kept

parts.note: a butt is the buttocks, one's rear end
the pectoral muscles sit on the chest

explanation.surface: A gym-goer boasts that a bulky backside and chest make them the most manly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear end' sounds anatomical in the surface and it is, but as a slangy American word for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchest is the superlative of butch, meaning the most aggressively masculine.

clue.text: We're told of shelter in a field

indicators.note: what we are told we hear, so the answer sounds like the word

parts.note: a lee is a sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: Someone reports a hut standing in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: LEA is a poetic word for a meadow, and LEE (shelter, as in the lee of a wall) sounds just the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is an open grassy field or meadow.

clue.text: Kit swears wildly, has fun on a lake?

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about wildly into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone called Kit curses furiously and then enjoys a day on the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Kit reads as a person's name, but it is just three letters of fodder; the question mark marks the definition as one example of having fun on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who water-skis is towed across a lake for fun.

clue.text: Father Ted's Jewish counterpart went on?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a Jewish equivalent of the priest Father Ted would be ...
second meaning: talked at tedious length

explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is a British TV sitcom about an Irish Catholic priest; swap the priest's title for a rabbi's and you get the answer split as RABBI TED. The question mark flags that 'went on' needs 'on' supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit, British slang from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk, means to chatter on and on.

clue.text: Irrational, as the nastiest numbers?

indicators.note: the letters stop making sense, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A maths quip about which numbers are the most irrational and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Irrational' and 'numbers' together, the clue sounds like maths, but a numb-er here is something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaesthetists numb patients before surgery, so they are literally numbers.

clue.text: Modern experimental facility sent back curry

indicators.note: what is sent back is returned, so read it right to left

parts.note: an IT lab, a computer laboratory

explanation.surface: A trendy test kitchen returns a curry to the chef.
explanation.walkthrough: Sending food back in a restaurant is the surface; the curry in question is itself the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a curry cooked and served in a wok-like metal bowl, a Birmingham favourite.

clue.text: Swap short amount of time — about time! — for confidential info

parts.note: to trade is to swap
SEC is short for second, a brief time
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone impatiently swapping a moment for secret information.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade secret is a method or formula a business keeps private from competitors.

clue.text: Most of words rejected; Everyman's beginning to get tired

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards
most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: the possessive ending 's of the setter's name supplies the letter S

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of Everyman's

explanation.surface: The setter rejects most of the wording and begins to flag.
explanation.walkthrough: The S comes from the possessive 's of Everyman's; 'Most of' trims WORDS to WORD and 'rejected' turns it to DROW.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze or grow sleepy is to start to feel tired and nod off.

clue.text: This restaurant'll advertise tasty tapenades, olives, ricotta — Italian antipasti — you'll want the starters!

definitions.text: This restaurant'll advertise tasty tapenades, olives, ricotta — Italian antipasti — you'll want the starters!

indicators.note: the starters of words are their first letters

parts.words: This restaurant'll advertise tasty tapenades, olives, ricotta — Italian antipasti
parts.note: first letters of the nine words

explanation.surface: A menu blurb for an Italian place boasting of its antipasti.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description: 'the starters' is a restaurant word for first courses, and also for first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian restaurant, the sort that would serve these antipasti.

clue.text: In sum, I might be one of these?

definitions.meaning: the surface reads I as the speaker, taking part in a total; the setter means the letter I as it appears written in a sum
the surface wonders whether the speaker belongs to a group; the setter means the letter I stands for the number one

explanation.surface: A person wondering whether they count as one of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' reads as the speaker, but it is the letter I, which is the Roman numeral for one, in a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman numerals are the letters I, V, X, L, C, D and M used as numbers, and I is one of them.

clue.text: Plain and somewhat porcellanous

indicators.note: only some of the word is used

parts.note: porcel(LANO)us, hidden in the middle

explanation.surface: Describing a pale, porcelain-like face as plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain reads as an adjective, homely, but it is the noun: a grassy plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a wide grassy plain in Spanish America.

clue.text: One rambling, greeting king and queen once

parts.note: hi, a greeting
K for king, as in chess
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A chatterbox who once met the king and queen and won't stop talking about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rambling suggests talking on and on; here it means walking in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling is the British word for leisurely country walking, so a rambler is a plain synonym for this walker.

clue.text: City playing United, twice — plural — a matey kickaround, at first

indicators.note: playing signals that the letters are being played about with and rearranged

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names
twice says the U for United is used two times
taken as written

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: first letter of matey
first letter of kickaround

explanation.surface: A sports report: a city side plays United twice, with plural friendly matches played among mates.
explanation.walkthrough: The pool is U, U, PLURAL, A, M and K, which rearranges into the eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuala Lumpur is the capital city of Malaysia.

clue.text: Powerful scent: a billionaire's characteristic?

definitions.note: 'Powerful scent' describes the quality muskiness, a noun for the smell's character
definitions.meaning: the heavy animal smell of musk, used in perfumes
the quality of being like Elon Musk, the billionaire, with a noun-making suffix on his surname

explanation.surface: A perfume advert suggesting a strong scent is the mark of the super-rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a joke on Elon Musk, the billionaire: Musk-iness is being like Musk.
explanation.definitionFit: Muskiness is the heavy, powerful smell of musk.

clue.text: Small Houyhnhnm, one hiding actual intentions?

parts.note: S for small, as on clothing labels
the Houyhnhnms are the talking horses of Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A little horse from Swift's satire that keeps its real motives to itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The Houyhnhnms are the rational, speaking horses Gulliver meets in Jonathan Swift's book.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalking-horse is a person or thing used to conceal someone's real plans, originally a horse hunters hid behind.

clue.text: No coal tar involved in type of surgery

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up, involved with each other

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A reassurance that no coal tar is used in some operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Coal tar sounds like a medical ingredient, which keeps the surface in the surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Root canal treatment is dental surgery on the pulp inside a tooth.

clue.text: Green tea brewed for youngster

indicators.note: brewing mixes the ingredients, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Making a cup of green tea for a young person.
explanation.walkthrough: Brewed fits the tea so snugly that it is easy to miss as an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a youngster aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: An entrée with cured cod announced where soldiers get fit?

indicators.note: what is announced is spoken, so the answer sounds like the words

parts.note: an entrée is a course, and cod that is cured is salt cod

explanation.surface: A waiter announces a starter of salt cod.
explanation.walkthrough: The dining-room surface hides an army training ground: say 'a salt course' quickly and it becomes ASSAULT COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the obstacle ground of walls, nets and ditches is exactly where army recruits build fitness.

clue.text: Carry, with difficulty, a little kitsch leprechaun

indicators.note: only a little of the words is used

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone lugging a tacky garden-ornament leprechaun about.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after Carry makes 'with difficulty' part of the definition, not a separate instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To schlep is to haul something heavy or awkward, from Yiddish.

clue.text: Many like a society without aristocrats

definitions.meaning: a society lacking counts, the noble title, read as the title plus a suffix meaning without

explanation.surface: A remark that many people would like to live in a society with no nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word: a society with no counts is count-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Countless means too many to count.

clue.text: Kind of song that brings illumination

definitions.note: 'Kind of song' is a noun phrase; TORCH works as the modifier in 'torch song'
definitions.meaning: a sentimental ballad of unrequited love
a hand-held light; in Britain, a flashlight

explanation.surface: A song that is enlightening.
explanation.walkthrough: A torch song is a sentimental ballad of unrequited love; in Britain a torch is also a flashlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch gives light, and a torch song is a lovelorn ballad.

clue.text: Replace a partner's copper vessel

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Swapping out a colleague's copper pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as a possessive but is a link (partner's = partner is); on the dance floor, to cut in is to take over someone's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in is to interrupt a dancing couple and take one partner's place.

clue.text: Outcast's check rejected

indicators.note: what is rejected is turned back, so read it right to left

parts.note: to check an attack is to repel it

explanation.surface: An outcast's cheque bounces.
explanation.walkthrough: Check reads as a bank cheque that bounces; it is the verb, to hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper, figuratively, is someone shunned by others.

clue.text: Exotic tanginess getting act of approval

indicators.note: the letters are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A food critic gives the thumbs-up to an unusual sharp flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSENTING here is a noun, the act of agreeing, which is why the definition is 'act of approval' rather than a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerund used as a noun: the verb assent means agree, so its -ing form names the act of giving approval.

clue.text: Sit fast, regularly dismissing uncertainties

indicators.note: dismiss every other letter at regular intervals

parts.note: s(I)t (F)a(S)t: keep the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Stand firm and brush aside all doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: Sit fast reads as an instruction to hold firm; it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifs, as in 'no ifs or buts', are doubts or uncertainties.

clue.text: Procure leverage

definitions.meaning: noun: a firm grip or foothold that lets you apply force

explanation.walkthrough: Leverage reads as a verb beside Procure, but it is the noun: getting a purchase on a lid means getting a grip on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are plain synonyms, one verb (buy) and one the older mechanical noun sense of a grip for applying force.

clue.text: Nearer the end

definitions.meaning: comparative of close, said with a hard S
something that closes, like the last song of a show, said with a Z sound

explanation.walkthrough: Two pronunciations: CLOSE-er with a hard S means nearer, while a CLOZE-er is what ends something, like the last song in a set.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer means nearer, and a closer is the final item or act.
